Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Body, health & movement

feel verb

well or ill

also how do you feel?, feel fine

classical

Cic. Att. 12.37.1: Pīliam et Atticam plānē bellē sē habēre
Traupman 98: sē male (bene) habēre

sē habēre (bene, male, melius)

feel (well, ill, better)

With an adverb: bene, male, melius mē habeō. For “feel” with an adjective Latin mostly uses esse: fessus sum, I feel tired.

Examples

  • ut prīmum gravitātem urbis excessī et illum odōrem culīnārum fūmantium … prōtinus mūtātam valētūdinem sēnsī

    as soon as I had left the heavy air of the city and that smell of smoking kitchens … I felt better at onceSen. Ep. 104.6

  • sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō. valētūdinem tuam velim cūrēs dīligentissimē.

    If you are well, good; I am well. Please take the greatest care of your health.Cic. Fam. 14.8.1

Other words

  • valeō, valēre, valuī — be well, feel well

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō; Traupman 98: minus valeō, melius valeō

    Minus valeō, I’m not so well; melius valeō, I feel better. Cicero’s letters open Sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō.

See also I don’t feel well, I feel better, how are you?, I’m fine, feel, hurt.
